claims.text: Friction stir welding or localized friction stir processing can be used to rejoin the damaged regions of the component.
Friction stir repair produces a dynamically recrystallized microstructural zone.
Friction stir repair produces a refined microstructural zone.
Friction stir repair reduces residual stresses.
Friction stir repair lowers the likelihood of forming deleterious brittle phases.
Friction stir welding is a solid-state process that avoids melting.
Avoiding melting prevents the formation of brittle phases that induce hot cracking.
Mechanical stirring and plastic deformation refine the microstructure.
Mechanical stirring and plastic deformation homogenize residual stresses.
Microstructural refinement and residual-stress homogenization enhance joint integrity.
A friction-stir-repaired component will have improved or comparable joint strength relative to a fusion-weld-repaired component.
A friction-stir-repaired component will have enhanced ductility relative to a fusion-weld-repaired component.
A friction-stir-repaired component will have superior resistance to hot cracking relative to a fusion-weld-repaired component.
Traditional fusion-welding repair typically induces hot cracking in the targeted class of materials.
Traditional fusion-welding repair produces associated microstructural and mechanical defects in the targeted class of materials.
The proposed friction stir repair remains effective under significant thermal cycling and mechanical stresses.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the specific material properties and operating conditions.
